description:
We are a team from FPT University, bringing together Software Engineering and Data Science to turn complex environmental data into practical solutions.

For NASA Space Apps, we are building TerraCycle AI with a clear ambition: make Earth observation data more accessible and useful to the people working closest to the land. Our interests span artificial intelligence, data analytics, backend engineering, and human-centered design, united by a commitment to solving meaningful real-world problems.
summary:
TerraCycle AI is a climate-adaptive crop-rotation decision-support prototype developed for the NASA Space Apps Field Shift challenge. It helps farmers explore crop choices as growing conditions change by combining NASA POWER historical climate data, traceable crop requirements, and locally supplied soil and water information.

Our web application compares rotation options involving rice, maize, mung bean, and soybean, considering planting periods, temperature, soil suitability, salinity, and water availability. Users can explore priorities such as water conservation and soil recovery, review the reasoning behind each option, and identify missing information before making decisions. The system clearly distinguishes historical observations from forecasts and flags uncertainty when evidence is incomplete.

TerraCycle AI addresses the challenge by translating Earth observation data into understandable, farm-level planning support. This matters because changing rainfall, heat, and salinity can make familiar cropping patterns less suitable. By making alternatives and their limitations easier to assess, the project supports more informed decisions toward resilient agriculture.
details:
TerraCycle AI is a web-based decision-support prototype that helps farmers explore crop rotations under changing climate conditions. Developed for the Field Shift challenge, it connects historical climate observations with crop requirements and local farm information to make rotation planning more understandable and transparent.

What it does and how it works

Users provide their farm location, current crop, intended planting date, soil information, and water availability. They can compare options according to priorities such as maintaining current practices, conserving water, or supporting soil recovery.

The prototype evaluates rice, maize, mung bean, and soybean using:

  • NASA POWER historical climate data, including temperature and precipitation.
  • Traceable crop requirements and rotation compatibility rules.
  • Farmer-provided soil pH, soil salinity, irrigation access, and irrigation-water salinity.
  • Planting calendars and crop growth durations where verified information is available.

The application explains why an option is potentially suitable, unsuitable, or uncertain. It also identifies missing measurements and provides source references so users can understand the evidence behind the assessment.

Benefits and intended impact

TerraCycle AI aims to help farmers and agricultural advisers make better-informed decisions about crop diversification. It makes climate and crop information easier to interpret while highlighting constraints that need attention before planting.

Its intended impact is to support climate-resilient agriculture, more thoughtful water management, and consideration of rotations that include legumes. These are planning objectives; the prototype does not claim measured improvements in yield, water savings, or soil restoration.

Tools and technologies

We developed the interface using React, TypeScript, and Vite. The backend uses Python and FastAPI, while the data-processing and assessment components use Python and pandas. The project includes NASA POWER data processing, an optional SoilGrids adapter, and an ECOCROP data-normalization adapter. Crop information and rotation rules are maintained in traceable JSON reference files.

We use pytest for automated checks and GitHub Actions to run tests and build the frontend. The prototype runs on standard computers and does not require specialized hardware.

Creativity and design considerations

The project’s creative approach is to turn climate data into an explainable comparison of farming choices. Instead of presenting a single unexplained recommendation, it shows alternatives, constraints, supporting evidence, and information gaps.

Our team considered differences between annual and seasonal measurements, local planting calendars, crop compatibility, water access, and the distinction between soil salinity and irrigation-water salinity. We also designed the system to preserve uncertainty: historical observations are never presented as forecasts, unavailable data remains explicitly unknown, and suitability scores are withheld when the evidence is insufficient. This makes transparency a central part of the user experience.
